title: MySQL/MariaDB

personasSubtitle: CRUD based on gsSpGetAllPersonas, gsSpInsertPersona, gsSpUpdatePersona, and gsQDeletePersona.
emptyRequest: This endpoint does not require a request body.
emptyResponse: The endpoint did not return content.

name: Name

operationDescriptions.default: This case shows how Generate Service publishes a MySQL/MariaDB source as a REST endpoint while preserving the generated signature.
operationDescriptions.gsSpGetAllPersonas: This case shows that Generate Service can expose a procedure without input and transform the complete persona result set into a REST list.
operationDescriptions.gsSpGetPersona: This case shows an id lookup through a procedure. The client sends pIdPersona and receives the typed rows returned by MySQL/MariaDB.
operationDescriptions.gsSpGetPersonasByEstado: This case shows a boolean filter in a procedure. MySQL/MariaDB returns SQL aliases and Generate Service publishes them as camelCase REST fields.
operationDescriptions.gsSpInsertPersona: This case shows an INSERT procedure without OUT parameters. Generate Service responds with a boolean when execution finishes without an exception.
operationDescriptions.gsSpUpdatePersona: This case shows an update procedure with scalar parameters and a boolean execution response.
operationDescriptions.gsSpInsertSelectPersona: This case shows an INSERT plus SELECT flow. The client creates a persona and receives the inserted row in the same response.
operationDescriptions.gsSpUpdateSelectPersona: This case shows an UPDATE plus SELECT flow. The client updates and receives the final persona state from MySQL/MariaDB.
operationDescriptions.gsSpMultiResultPersona: This case shows that Generate Service can materialize multiple MySQL/MariaDB procedure result sets: persona detail and aggregate summary.
operationDescriptions.gsSpMultiOperationPersona: This case shows a procedure with several internal operations: insert, update, and finally return the resulting row.
operationDescriptions.gsSpInsertPersonaJson: This case shows that MySQL/MariaDB can receive JSON and Generate Service lets REST clients send it as a natural object through @RawJson.
operationDescriptions.gsSpInsertPersonasJsonArray: This case shows a bulk load from a natural JSON array. MySQL/MariaDB processes it with JSON_TABLE and the API returns boolean if no error occurs.
operationDescriptions.gsSpGetPersonaJson: This case shows that a MySQL/MariaDB JSON output is delivered to the client as natural JSON, not escaped text.
operationDescriptions.gsSpGetPersonasJsonArray: This case shows that JSON_ARRAYAGG can build a JSON array in MySQL/MariaDB and Generate Service publishes it as a natural REST array.
operationDescriptions.gsSpInsertJsonResultset: This case shows a mixed flow: receive natural JSON, return one result set with parsed values, and another with the inserted row.
operationDescriptions.gsSpCountPersonasOut: This case shows a procedure with a scalar OUT parameter for publishing database counts in a simple REST response.
operationDescriptions.gsSpGetPersonaResumenOut: This case shows multiple OUT parameters in one procedure, combining text, number, boolean, and registration date.
operationDescriptions.gsSpGetMysqlTiposExtraOut: This case shows additional MySQL/MariaDB types: DECIMAL, TEXT, TIMESTAMP, TIME, VARBINARY, and JSON in one response DTO.
operationDescriptions.gsSpIncrementarEdadInout: This case shows a numeric INOUT parameter: REST sends an initial value and receives the value changed by MySQL/MariaDB.
operationDescriptions.gsSpNormalizarEmailInout: This case shows a text INOUT parameter that normalizes data inside the database and returns the final value to the client.
operationDescriptions.gsSpInsertPersonaOutId: This case shows an INSERT that returns the MySQL/MariaDB generated id through an OUT parameter.
operationDescriptions.gsSpUpdatePersonaOutCount: This case shows an update that returns ROW_COUNT through an OUT parameter to report affected rows.
operationDescriptions.gsSpInsertPersonaOutResultset: This case shows an INSERT with an id OUT parameter and an additional result set, useful for confirming creation and returning the row.
operationDescriptions.gsSpGetPersonaRequired: This case shows a controlled business rule with SIGNAL. If the persona does not exist, MySQL/MariaDB propagates the error to the generated endpoint.
operationDescriptions.gsSpUpdateMysqlTiposExtra: This case shows updates of additional MySQL/MariaDB types, including a JSON profile built from UI fields and binary content sent as base64.
operationDescriptions.gsFnDeletePersona: This case shows a MySQL/MariaDB function that runs DELETE and returns the affected row count as a scalar value.
operationDescriptions.fnPersonaJson: This case shows a function that returns JSON and Generate Service exposes it as natural JSON with @JsonRawValue.
operationDescriptions.gsFnGetPersonaNombre: This case shows a scalar read function that returns a full name calculated by MySQL/MariaDB.
operationDescriptions.gsFnGetPersonaFechaNacimiento: This case shows DATE mapping from a MySQL/MariaDB function to a REST response.
operationDescriptions.gsFnGetPersonaFechaRegistro: This case shows DATETIME/TIMESTAMP mapping from a MySQL/MariaDB function to REST.
operationDescriptions.gsFnGetMysqlTiposExtraSalario: This case shows DECIMAL returned as BigDecimal for monetary or precision values.
operationDescriptions.gsFnGetMysqlTiposExtraHoraContacto: This case shows TIME returned as a string in the generated REST contract.
operationDescriptions.gsFnGetMysqlTiposExtraBio: This case shows TEXT returned from MySQL/MariaDB as a REST string.
operationDescriptions.gsFnCountPersonas: This case shows a function with no input returning a scalar count for REST clients.
operationDescriptions.gsFnInsertPersonasJson: This case shows a DML function that receives a natural JSON array, inserts several personas, and returns the last generated id.
operationDescriptions.gsFnUpdatePersona: This case shows a DML update function that returns boolean to indicate whether a row changed.
operationDescriptions.gsQPersonaById: This case shows that Generate Service can publish a parameterized SELECT query as a REST endpoint without creating a procedure or function.
operationDescriptions.gsQMysqlTiposExtraByPersona: This case shows a query over additional MySQL/MariaDB types, returning DECIMAL, TEXT, TIMESTAMP, TIME, VARBINARY, and JSON.
operationDescriptions.gsQPersonasByNombre: This case shows a text search with LIKE and CONCAT. The client sends a name fragment and receives typed matches.
operationDescriptions.gsQPersonasByActivo: This case shows a direct boolean filter in SQL query form and a response ready for UI display.
operationDescriptions.gsQPersonasSelfJoinActivo: This case shows that a self join query can also be generated as a REST endpoint to compare rows in the same table.
operationDescriptions.gsQPersonasActivasWith: This case shows a query with WITH/CTE to separate filtering logic before returning the result.
operationDescriptions.gsQPersonasStatsExtraWith: This case shows an aggregate query with CTE and LEFT JOIN, combining personas with salaries from the extra table.
operationDescriptions.gsQMysqlTiposExtraByPerfilJson: This case shows filtering by a property inside MySQL/MariaDB JSON using JSON_EXTRACT and returning natural JSON to the client.
operationDescriptions.gsQInsertPersona: This case shows an INSERT query generated as a POST endpoint. The response is boolean when the statement runs without exception.
operationDescriptions.gsQInsertPersonaSelect: This case shows INSERT based on SELECT, where the client sends variable values and MySQL/MariaDB completes other fields from a base persona.
operationDescriptions.gsQUpdatePersona: This case shows a parameterized UPDATE query published as a REST endpoint with boolean response.
operationDescriptions.gsQUpdateMysqlTiposExtra: This case shows an UPDATE query over extra types, including a JSON profile built from UI fields and VARBINARY/base64 in the generated contract.
operationDescriptions.gsQDeletePersona: This case shows a parameterized DELETE query. The client sends idPersona and Generate Service returns boolean when execution succeeds.

support.title: MySQL/MariaDB Support
support.subtitle: Guide to procedures, functions, SQL queries, result sets, JSON, and additional MySQL/MariaDB types published by Generate Service.
support.jsonSubtitle: The MySQL/MariaDB suite uses JSON and functions such as JSON_EXTRACT, JSON_OBJECT, JSON_ARRAYAGG, and JSON_TABLE to read, build, and transform documents.
support.jsonRawNote: Generate Service maps JSON to String in Java, but DTOs use @RawJson on input and @JsonRawValue on output. The UI therefore sends and receives natural JSON objects or arrays, not escaped JSON strings.
support.capabilitiesSubtitle: The MySQL/MariaDB catalog covers procedures with IN/OUT/INOUT, scalar functions, SQL queries, multiple result sets, DML, JSON, and a scoped set of types confirmed for the generated contract.
support.typeMappingTitle: MySQL/MariaDB types supported by Generate Service
support.typeMappingSubtitle: Scoped mapping table between MySQL/MariaDB types and the generated Java/REST contract. JSON stays separate because of its raw handling.
support.typeMappingNote: This table documents only the MySQL/MariaDB types used or confirmed for this suite and its Generate Service contract. JSON is shown separately because the Java contract handles it as String with raw serialization. MySQL/MariaDB is not documented here with ARRAY or typed scalar lists: contract lists belong to result sets materialized as row DTOs.
support.rulesSubtitle: These rules apply to the generated microservice and help keep the client-facing contract stable.

nativeJson.title: JSON type
nativeJson.description: MySQL/MariaDB receives JSON directly in procedures and functions, and Generate Service detects it as a raw field in the generated DTO.

jsonOperators.title: Reading inside MySQL/MariaDB
jsonOperators.description: The suite uses JSON_EXTRACT, JSON_UNQUOTE, and JSON_TABLE to read properties, cast values, and process JSON arrays.

javaRaw.title: Java keeps raw String
javaRaw.description: The Java contract keeps String internally, while raw annotations serialize and deserialize real JSON.

naturalRest.title: Natural REST payload
naturalRest.description: Requests should send normal JSON objects or arrays; Generate Service performs the raw conversion into the internal String.

procedures.title: Procedures
procedures.description: Supports MySQL/MariaDB procedures with IN, OUT, and INOUT, including scalar responses, result sets, multiple result sets, and JSON.

functions.title: Functions
functions.description: Exposes MySQL/MariaDB read and DML functions with scalar returns as POST endpoints.

queries.title: SQL queries
queries.description: Free SQL queries are published as POST endpoints, including SELECT, JOIN, WITH/CTE, aggregates, INSERT, UPDATE, and DELETE.

resultSets.title: Result sets
resultSets.description: SELECT statements emitted by procedures are materialized as typed row DTO lists inside the response. This does not imply support for MySQL/MariaDB scalar lists.

jsonTypes.title: JSON
jsonTypes.description: JSON is exposed as dynamic JSON in REST through @RawJson and @JsonRawValue.

extraTypes.title: Extra MySQL/MariaDB types
extraTypes.description: The suite validates DECIMAL, TEXT, TIMESTAMP, TIME, VARBINARY, and JSON from table, procedure, function, and query in MySQL/MariaDB.

dmlQueries.title: DML queries
dmlQueries.description: INSERT, UPDATE, and DELETE generated as queries return boolean when execution finishes without exception.

errors.title: Controlled errors
errors.description: SIGNAL SQLSTATE demonstrates how a database rule is propagated to the generated REST endpoint.

rules.snakeCase: In MySQL/MariaDB, use snake_case for parameters, SQL aliases, and column names.
rules.camelCase: Generate Service converts MySQL/MariaDB names to camelCase for Java and the REST contract.
rules.endpointNames: Procedure, function, and query names become generated REST method and endpoint names.
rules.envOverride: The base URL for this catalog can be configured in .env with API_ENDPOINT_MYSQL; otherwise the UI defaults to http://localhost:8083. Backend REST paths can also be changed through environment variables.
rules.jsonProperty: Variable names exposed in JSON can be adjusted with Jackson @JsonProperty.

rules.repositoryIntegrity: Once the microservice is generated, Generate Service validates the integrity of generated repositories.
rules.licenseValidation: The generated API includes local integrity and license validations using a secure token emitted by Generate Service. These validations run inside the generated API and do not require external licensing calls.
rules.signedMetadata: Do not manually modify @Callable, @SpParameter, types, inputs, outputs, SQL name, or signed query.
rules.regenerateOnSourceChange: If the data source, procedure, function, query, parameters, or types change, regenerate the microservice.
rules.oneEndpointPerSource: Each procedure, function, or query intended for clients should be generated as its own stable API source.

rules.controllers: You can add controller logic to validate, adapt, or enrich input and output.
rules.services: You can add business logic in services before or after invoking the generated source.
rules.businessLogic: You can recalculate, compose, or transform the response without changing signed metadata.
rules.sourceLock: The generated data source is protected: repositories, signature, parameters, query, and source SQL are not manually modified.
